title: Collections Desk Guide: Delinquency Allowance on Retail Installment Contract Hardship Deferrals
content:
**Rule.** For a hardship extension agreement on a contract under Retail Installment Contracts, the delinquency allowance turns on the next due date, the signing date and the partial installment credit carried:

1. When the signing date is more than **10** days (the product's late-charge grace period) after the next due date **and** partial installment credit is carried, the allowance is the installments past due on the signing date — each monthly due date from the next due date through the signing date — plus the next installment to fall due.
2. When the next due date is on or after the signing date, the allowance is the tier's maximum installments deferred by one extension.
3. In every other case it is **one** installment.

| Days from the next due date to the signing date | Partial installment credit carried | Delinquency allowance |
|---|---|---|
| 0 or fewer (next due date on or after the signing date) | any | the tier's per-request maximum |
| 1 to 10 | any | one installment |
| more than 10 | none | one installment |
| more than 10 | some | installments past due on the signing date plus one |

## Worked counts (hypothetical contract, due day the 3rd)

- Next due date 3 March, signing 20 April, 50.00 of partial credit carried: 48 days after the next due date. The monthly due dates from 3 March through 20 April are 3 March and 3 April, 2 installments; plus the next to fall due (3 May), the allowance is 3.
- Next due date 3 March, signing 18 March, no partial credit: 15 days, but no partial credit, so one installment.
- Next due date 3 March, signing 3 March: the next due date is on the signing date, so the tier's per-request maximum.
- Next due date 3 March, signing 13 March with partial credit carried: 10 days is not more than 10, so one installment.
